derived_observations: The second-cycle divergence is already visible at Current Return, before Surplus or reinvestment: opponent Day8 G1 produces 12.0 non-WHEAT units during Day8-12 while self G1 produces 0, with the same direction in all 10 cases.
Total non-WHEAT production over Day8-12 is 56.0 opponent versus 18.3 self, so the Day8 starting thickness gap is not merely carried forward; it appears as a wider observed Return gap.
Cash-flow separation then widens further. Self sells 11681.0 total versus opponent 19545.1, while self operating BUY_PRODUCT WHEAT spend is higher: 7581.6 versus 4394.3 in all 10 cases.
As a result, surplus after operating is 4099.4 self versus 15150.8 opponent, a gap of 11051.4 in all 10 cases.
Productive spend is then 3494.9 self versus 9322.6 opponent, after which G2 physical future capacity is 28.4 versus 136.0 units, opponent ahead in all 10 cases.

Therefore the bridge does not identify a single late reinvestment failure. The first clear second-cycle separator is the transition from Day8 future cohort to observed Current Return, and downstream operating burden, surplus, productive spend, and G2 formation compound the gap.

A second large divergence exists between productive-spend magnitude and resulting G2 physical capacity, but this audit does not call it conversion efficiency because spend composition differs and Cash is fungible.
